Consider the following initial value problem for the functions $y=y(x),z=z(x),w=w(x):$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=(x+1)(y-1)+z,\, & y(0)=1 \\ {z}^{′}=2-(x-1)(z-2),\, & z(0)=2 \\ {w}^{′}=\sqrt{x+{w}^{2}}-\frac{y}{2},\, & w(0)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use Euler's Method with one step to approximate $y(1),$ $z(1),$ and $w(1).$

$\,y(1)≈$
{{field-1}},
$\,z(1)≈$
{{field-2}},
$\,w(1)≈$
{{field-3}}
worked_solution:
Euler's method approximates the solution of an initial value problem containing a system of ODEs by applying the update rule component-wise to each equation.

Since we want to find the value of $y$, $z$ and $w$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0=1.
$$

First, we place the initial condition data in a table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ |  |  | $2$ |  |  | $1$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′},$ ${z}^{′},$ and ${w}^{′}$ according to the given rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(x+1)(y-1)+z \\  & =(0+1)(1-1)+2 \\  & =2 \\ {z}^{′} & =2-(x-1)(z-2) \\  & =2-(0-1)(2-2) \\  & =2 \\ {w}^{′} & =\sqrt{x+{w}^{2}}-\frac{y}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{0+{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |  | $2$ | $2$ |  | $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy,$ $Δz,$ and $Δw$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2 \\ Δz & ={z}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2 \\ Δw & ={w}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |

To get the new values of $x,$ $y,$ $z,$ and $w$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x,$ $Δy$ to $y,$ $Δz$ to $z,$ and $Δw$ to $w,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=0+1=1 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=1+2=3 \\ {z}_{\text{new}} & =z+Δz=2+2=4 \\ {w}_{\text{new}} & =w+Δw=1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these values to our table in a new row gives the following:

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| $1$ | $3$ |  |  | $4$ |  |  | $\frac{3}{2}$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that
$y(1)≈3,$
$z(1)≈4,$
and
$w(1)≈\frac{3}{2}.$
